NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

SUMMARY
Senior cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including 6 years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud environments, infrastructure as code, and self-service platforms. Technical lead who helps product teams deliver reliable, observable services through sensible platform defaults, SLOs and clear incident processes.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, Linux
Infrastructure as code and platform engineering: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Argo CD, Helm, Kustomize, Karpenter
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Automation and testing: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions, Puppet, k6

EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer - Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS), Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 - present
- Technical lead for a 5-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform of 8 clusters and approximately 350 services across 3 regions.
- Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately 2 weeks to under 1 day.
- Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer - Brightwater Games, Leeds | Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and then EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules; used Atlantis to run plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Used k6 for pre-launch load testing and supported launch-day capacity planning.

Linux Systems Engineer - Pennine Hosting, Sheffield | Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science, University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native), Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. It uses quantified outcomes effectively: 8 EKS clusters, approximately 350 services, a 60% reduction in on-call pages, a 38% EC2 cost reduction, and a reduction in deployment lead time from approximately two weeks to under one day. The structure is concise, readable, and appropriate for a senior infrastructure contractor. The main content limitation is that several requirements in the role—system design, networking security, mTLS/TLS, practical security, and stakeholder alignment—are not evidenced. These are candidate-experience gaps or evidence gaps rather than general writing weaknesses.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard job titles, chronological experience, and abundant relevant AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, Linux, and automation keywords. It should parse reliably and has a strong AI-screening probability for the AWS/platform engineering portions of the role. The strongest ATS weakness is that Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, systems architecture, and system design are not present. They must not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience. The skills section is well organized into searchable categories, and the use of both expanded terms and tool names is helpful.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on AWS infrastructure operation, Kubernetes platform engineering, infrastructure as code, reliability, observability, Linux, technical leadership, and supporting product teams. The candidate's internal developer platform, self-service provisioning, SLOs, incident processes, and technical lead experience are relevant to Corvale's engineering-led, end-to-end ownership culture. However, the candidate information does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, train/vehicle connectivity, IoT or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, or explicit security engineering. The CV also provides limited direct evidence of formal systems architecture or bringing external stakeholders such as manufacturers along. These are genuine alignment gaps and should not be represented as achieved requirements.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the SUMMARY section, replace the broad sentence "Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud environments, infrastructure as code, and self-service platforms" with a more evidence-based version such as: "Experienced building and operating AWS cloud infrastructure, Terraform-managed environments, Kubernetes platforms, and self-service developer platforms." This keeps the role's terminology while tying the claim directly to the documented experience.

2. In the SUMMARY section, make the technical-lead evidence more explicit by changing "Technical lead who helps product teams deliver reliable, observable services through sensible platform defaults, SLOs and clear incident processes" to: "Technical lead helping product teams deliver reliable, observable services through platform defaults, self-service provisioning, SLOs, error budgets and clear incident processes." These terms are supported by the Tallybrook experience and improve alignment with the requirement to support backend developers.

3. In the EXPERIENCE section under Tallybrook Ltd, change "Technical lead for a 5-person platform team" to "Technical lead for a 5-person platform team, operating AWS infrastructure and an EKS platform across 8 clusters, approximately 350 services and 3 regions." This consolidates the leadership and hands-on infrastructure evidence in one ATS- and recruiter-friendly bullet without adding unsupported claims.

4. In the CORE SKILLS section, retain Terraform as a prominent standalone keyword and do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security engineering, IoT, automotive, or JVM technologies unless they are supported by additional verified experience. The current CV should not imply coverage of those requirements.
